preamble: A front-gliding diphthong [eɪ]/[ɛi] reduces to schwa [ə] in unstressed position. In English this happens in the unstressed final element of words like always, which American speakers pronounce /ˈɔlweɪz/ or /ˈɔlwəz/. Northumbrian English reduces the -day of weekday names and yesterday to [-də], where Northern England has full /-deɪ/.

examples.note: General American variant with the unstressed diphthong reduced to schwa; /ˈɔl.wɪz/ also occurs.
Northumbrian English reduces unstressed -day to [də]; likewise Sunday /ˈsʊn.də/ and yesterday /ˈjɪstədə/.
